Accessibility is non-negotiable. Everyone should be able to participate.
Keyboard navigation everywhere (Tab/Shift+Tab) Visible focus rings and skip links Sufficient color contrast (WCAG AA minimum) ARIA labels for icons and controls
Respect prefers-reduced-motion Offer a toggle to disable decorative effects
Write clear, jargon-free labels Avoid color as the only signal Provide alt text for imagery
Associate labels and inputs Describe errors inline and conversationally Prevent accidental destructive actions
Screen reader pass (NVDA, VoiceOver) Keyboard-only pass Color-blindness simulation Accessible governance is just governance that includes everyone.
This section outlines how we structure UI, flows, and state for a clear, maintainable, and extensible front end.

App shell: navigation, footer, global effects, layout Pages: Swap, Governance, AltarBurn, Donate, Contact Domain modals: Treasury, DAO, NFT, Oracle, Admin Primitives: buttons, cards, inputs, typography Effects: spores, sparkles, mist, cursor trails Icons: SVG sets with subtle animations

Fetch/init session state (wallet, network) Render page info (context, warnings, how-to) Render domain UI (forms, charts, actions) Render modals for complex/confirm flows Collect analytics and event telemetry (privacy-respecting)

UI state via React hooks (local) and lightweight contexts (global) Async services wrapped in single-responsibility functions Side-effects gated by confirmations and preflight checks Error boundaries + toasts/modals for feedback
Disable actions when preconditions unmet (no wallet, wrong network) Confirmations for any on-chain mutation Explicit gas and network context shown to user Clear rollback and failure states
CSS Modules for scoped styles Respect reduced motion preference Theming via CSS variables (light/dark support)
Keyboard-first interactions, focus rings ARIA labels for icons and actions High contrast defaults
Content through message maps Avoid hard-coded strings in logic
Non-PII analytics: page views, success rates, error classes Feature flags for incremental rollout
Name components by domain (e.g., TreasuryProposalModal) Keep components pure; push side effects to hooks/services Encapsulate Web3 calls in adapters Prefer composition over inheritance
src/ components/ pages/ modals/ ui/ icons/ effects/ hooks/ services/ styles/ This keeps domain code discoverable and cohesive. Add new features by composing these layers.

We hold safety as sacred. The front end is a critical security boundary.
Never handle secrets or private keys client-side Fail safe: default to no action unless conditions are met Make dangerous actions obvious and deliberate
Wallets: user-owned, we only request signatures when necessary Contracts: addresses hardcoded per-network via allowlists RPC: prefer reputable endpoints + fallbacks
Sanitize and validate all user inputs Display amounts with clear units and rounding rules Detect and prevent copy/paste typos where possible
Always show contract names/addresses clearly Link to explorers with checksum addresses Consider ENS where appropriate, but verify
Lock dependency versions; watch advisories Prefer audited libraries for crypto primitives Avoid dynamic code execution
Emergency banner and kill-switch flags Known-good build rollback plan Public postmortems with action items Protect the flock. Communicate clearly. Move carefully when funds are at stake.
Keep state simple, predictable, and close to where it's used.
Local state with React useState/useReducer Shared state via small, focused Contexts (wallet, theme, network) Derived state via selectors/memos Async state via hooks that return {data, loading, error}
SessionContext: wallet address, chainId, connection status NetworkContext: RPC health, gas price, explorer URLs FeatureFlagsContext: enable/disable experimental flows
Isolate API/Web3 effects in hooks (e.g., useSwap, useGovernance) Debounce expensive operations Cancel inflight requests on unmount
Persist only non-sensitive preferences (theme, dismissed banners) Never persist secrets or private data
function useProposalList() { const [state, setState] = useState({list: [], loading: true, error: null}); useEffect(() => { /* fetch, set, catch */ }, []); return state; }
Unit test reducers and hooks in isolation Mock providers and network calls Verify loading/error UI states Keep it boring. Boring state is reliable state.
We test to protect people and treasuries, not just code.

Critical flows: connect wallet, network switch, submit proposal, make offering, swap Error states: wrong network, rejection, insufficient funds, RPC down Accessibility: tabbability, ARIA labels, color contrast Visual regressions (optional): snapshot of critical components
React Testing Library: behavior-focused tests Jest/Vitest: unit and integration tests MSW: mock network requests
Mock provider/wallet in test harness Render components with minimal viable context Prefer user-centric assertions (visible text, roles)
describe('Governance', () => { it('renders proposals and handles vote', async () => { // mock proposals // render <Governance /> // expect list, click vote, assert confirmation }); });
Run tests on PRs Fail fast on flake by reducing reliance on timeouts
Test on mobile devices and slow networks Verify explorer links and post-tx UX Test what matters most to the community. Confidence is a feature.
Common issues and how to resolve them quickly.

Not detecting wallet: ensure a Web3-capable browser or install MetaMask Stuck on wrong network: use the network switch button in the banner Transactions failing: check gas settings, balances, and contract addresses
Slow animations: enable Reduced Motion in settings or OS preferences Layout issues on mobile: clear cache, verify viewport meta present Images not loading: check CDN cache and path case-sensitivity

To the world, generosity often means giving up — a kind of loss or sacrifice. But as A Course in Miracles reveals: "To the world, generosity means 'giving away' in the sense of 'giving up.' To the teachers of God, it means giving away in order to keep. But he does want to keep for himself all things that are of God, and therefore for His Son. These he can give away in true generosity, protecting them forever for himself." (ACIM, M-4.VII.1:4-5;2:10,12) True generosity arises not from sacrifice but from Self-interest rightly understood — the kind of interest that seeks only what cannot be lost. "The teacher of God is generous out of Self interest. This does not refer, however, to the self of which the world speaks. The teacher of God does not want anything he cannot give away, because he realizes it would be valueless to him by definition. What would he want it for? He could only lose because of it. He could not gain. Therefore he does not seek what only he could keep, because that is a guarantee of loss." (ACIM, M-4.VII.2:1-7) In this light, an Ethereal Offering is never a giving up but a giving through — a circulation of divine inheritance that enriches giver and receiver as one.
documents.s: What does "Ethereal Offering" mean in spiritual terms?

documents.t: "It is not sacrifice to wake to glory. But it is sacrifice to accept anything less than glory. Learn that you must be worthy of the Prince of Peace, born in you in honor of Him Whose host you are." (ACIM, T-15.III.8:2-4) "Sacrifice of any kind is nothing but a limitation imposed on giving." (ACIM, T-15.X.2:6) "No sacrifice of any kind, of anyone, is asked by Him." (ACIM, T-15.XI.2:4) "In His Presence the whole idea of sacrifice loses all meaning." (ACIM, T-15.XI.2:5) "The lesson I was born to teach… is that sacrifice is nowhere and love is everywhere. Let us join in celebrating peace by demanding no sacrifice of anyone, for so you offer me the love I offer you." (ACIM, T-15.XI.7:5;8:2-3) Thus, an Ethereal Offering is not a transaction of loss but a translation of love — the remembering that to give is to recognize we are deprived of nothing. "Peace is extended from you only to the eternal, and it reaches out from the eternal in you. It flows across all else." (ACIM, T-19.IV-B.4:1-2)

Within Ethereal Offering, this principle becomes a living system of circulation rather than accumulation: 💎 Transparent Giving Replaces Sacrifice Every contribution to the Ethereal Offering ecosystem is tracked transparently on-chain, ensuring that what is given flows visibly through the network. This transparency transforms giving from an act of blind faith into a witnessed circulation of value. When we can see where our offering goes and how it multiplies through the community, you realize you haven't lost anything — you've set something in motion that returns to you in countless forms. 🔐 Soulbound Gratitude Tokens Mirror Eternal Gifts Our Gratitude Tokens are soulbound — they cannot be traded, sold, or transferred. They represent recognition for authentic service, recovery, and contribution that stays with you forever. These tokens mirror the spiritual principle that what is truly valuable cannot be taken away. They are not commodities but permanent witnesses to the love you've extended. Just as spiritual gifts are eternal and cannot be lost, soulbound tokens remain with you as a testament to our participation in the sacred economy of giving. 🕊️ Zero-Knowledge Generosity Honors Privacy While Extending Trust Through zero-knowledge proofs, participants can give, vote, and contribute anonymously while still maintaining verifiable integrity. This honors the spiritual teaching that true generosity doesn't seek recognition or praise — it simply extends itself. The technology allows you to give without attachment to identity or reputation, while the network still validates the authenticity of our offering. Privacy becomes not a hiding place, but a sacred space where the ego's need for credit dissolves, and pure giving can emerge. 🌐 DAO Stewardship Ensures Continuous Return Our DAO governance model ensures that no offering is withheld but continually returned to the whole. Every decision made by the community reflects the principle of regenerative circulation. Funds flow toward healing initiatives, policy reform, and community support — then return as strengthened networks, expanded capacity, and renewed purpose. The DAO operates on the understanding that what serves the whole serves each part, and what is given to the community is never lost but multiplied through collective stewardship.

documents.t: The world teaches that to give is to lose. But in truth, to give is to recognize what you already have — and what you have cannot be diminished by sharing. When you give from the eternal (love, truth, compassion), you discover that these qualities grow stronger through extension. The more you give, the more you have.

The ego seeks what it alone can possess. But the Spirit seeks only what can be given away — because only what can be shared is truly valuable. This is Self-interest rightly understood: the recognition that our deepest fulfillment comes not from accumulation but from circulation, not from hoarding but from offering.
documents.s: 💫 True Self-Interest Seeks Only What Can Be Shared

documents.t: In the Ethereal Offering ecosystem, every act of giving is simultaneously an act of receiving. When you contribute to the treasury, you receive governance rights. When you serve the community, you receive soulbound recognition. When you vote anonymously, you receive the gift of collective wisdom. The boundary between giver and receiver dissolves, revealing the truth that all giving is a form of receiving, and all receiving is a form of giving.

Water doesn't hoard itself — it flows, circulates, nourishes, and returns. Our tokenomics and governance structures are designed to mirror this natural law. Value is meant to move, not to stagnate. When it flows freely through transparent channels, it brings life wherever it goes. When it's dammed up in private wallets or centralized institutions, it becomes stagnant and loses its vitality. Ethereal Offering creates the channels for value to flow as it was meant to — in service of life, healing, and renewal.

What would it mean to give without the fear of loss? Consider: If you knew that everything you gave would return to you multiplied — not necessarily in the same form, but in value and meaning — how would that change what you're willing to offer? The Ethereal Offering invites you to experiment with this principle. Give our time, attention, service, or resources, and watch how the network responds. You may not receive back exactly what you gave, but you will receive something of equal or greater value: connection, recognition, purpose, or impact. What are you trying to keep that you cannot give away? The Course teaches that what we try to keep for ourselves alone becomes a "guarantee of loss." Reflect on what you're holding onto — whether it's knowledge, resources, time, or love — that you're afraid to share. What would happen if you released it into circulation? Often, what we hoard out of fear becomes a burden. What we give freely becomes a blessing — both to others and to ourselves. How does the platform help you practice generosity? Ethereal Offering is designed as a practice ground for sacred economics. Every interaction — voting, contributing, receiving tokens, participating in governance — is an opportunity to experience generosity as circulation rather than sacrifice. The transparency of the treasury lets you see our offerings in motion. The soulbound tokens remind you that what you've given can never be taken away. The zero-knowledge proofs free you from the ego's need for recognition. How might you use the platform not just as a tool, but as a spiritual practice?

"What can be more joyous than to perceive we are deprived of nothing?" (ACIM, T-15.XI.8:3) Generosity is not a moral obligation or a spiritual discipline to master. It is the natural expression of abundance — the recognition that you already have everything worth keeping, and that sharing it only increases its value. Ethereal Offering exists to make this truth tangible, visible, and experiential. Through transparent flows, soulbound recognition, and collective governance, we create a space where generosity becomes not just an ideal, but a living reality. Welcome to the sacred economy. Welcome to the circulation of love.

A crypto wallet is our digital identity on the blockchain. Our wallet address (e.g., 0x1234...5678) is public and used to receive tokens. Our private key is like our password—never share it! Recommended Wallets: MetaMask (browser extension & mobile) — metamask.io Rainbow (mobile-first, beautiful UX) — rainbow.me Coinbase Wallet (beginner-friendly) — wallet.coinbase.com Installation Steps: Visit the wallet's official website Download the browser extension or mobile app Create a new wallet CRITICAL: Write down our seed phrase (12-24 words) and store it safely offline Never share our seed phrase or private key with anyone

Gas is the fee paid to blockchain validators for processing our transactions. Think of it like postage for sending a letter. How to Get ETH: Buy on an exchange (Coinbase, Kraken, Binance) and withdraw to our wallet Use a faucet (for testnets only) — free small amounts for testing Receive from a friend — have them send to our wallet address How Much Do You Need? Psanctuary is a decentralized spiritual community advocating for religious freedom and the sacred use of entheogenic sacraments. We integrate ancient plant medicine wisdom with modern blockchain technology, creating a sovereign space for spiritual exploration, healing, and collective growth. Our mission is to preserve and protect the right to use sacred mushrooms as tools for consciousness expansion and divine connection.

A blockchain is a decentralized, immutable ledger that records transactions across a network of computers. For Psanctuary, this means our spiritual offerings, NFT collections, and governance votes are permanently recorded and cannot be censored or controlled by any central authority. It's the technological foundation for true digital sovereignty and religious freedom.
documents.s: 2. What is a Blockchain and Why Does It Matter?

documents.t: A crypto wallet (like MetaMask) is our digital identity on the blockchain. Our wallet address (e.g., 0x1234...5678) is like a bank account number—it's public and used to receive tokens. Our private key is like our password—never share it! Connect our wallet to interact with our dApp, sign transactions, and manage our digital assets.
documents.s: 3. What is a Wallet and How Do I Use It?

documents.t: Gas is the fee paid to blockchain validators for processing our transactions. Think of it like postage for sending a letter. On our platform, Daily Mushroom tokens (ERC-20) act as gas currency for cross-breeding, creating a self-sustaining ecosystem where our daily farming directly powers our genetic experiments.
documents.s: 4. What is Gas and Why Do I Need It?

documents.t: PSD is a stablecoin pegged to USD, designed for stable trading within the Ethereal Offering ecosystem. It's an ERC-20 token that maintains a 1:1 value with the US Dollar, providing a reliable medium of exchange for all platform transactions without the volatility of other cryptocurrencies.

ETHO is the primary governance and utility token of the Ethereal Offering platform. As an ERC-20 token, it's used for voting on proposals, burning at the altar for Proof of Burn NFTs, and participating in the ecosystem's economic activities. Holding ETHO gives you a voice in our decentralized spiritual community.

ERC-20 tokens (like ETHO, PSD, Daily Mushrooms) are fungible—each token is identical and divisible, like dollars. we can have 0.5 ETHO. ERC-721 tokens (like Mushroom Farm NFTs, Proof of Burn NFTs, Hybrid Mushrooms) are non-fungible—each is unique and indivisible, like a one-of-a-kind artwork or certificate. we can't have 0.5 of an NFT.
documents.s: 7. What's the difference between ERC-20 and ERC-721 tokens?

documents.t: Inoculate our substrate and mist regularly to maintain proper fruiting conditions. After colonization (8 hours), our first flush is ready! Harvest creates a unique ERC-721 NFT of our complete farm with multiple psilocybin mushrooms. Additionally, collect a single Daily Mushroom (ERC-20) every 24 hours—these act as gas currency for cross-breeding experiments.
documents.s: 8. How does the Mushroom Farm work?

documents.t: Cross-Breeding allows you to combine two parent mushrooms to create unique Hybrid Mushroom NFTs (ERC-721). Each breeding attempt consumes Daily Mushroom tokens (ERC-20) as gas, creating rare genetic combinations. It's like real mycology—experimenting with genetics to discover new strains and properties!

Like sublimation in alchemy, where matter transforms from solid to gas without passing through liquid, our ETHO tokens undergo a sacred transformation—transcending their material form to become eternal proof of our spiritual offering. This is the alchemical principle of releasing oneself from material attachment (magic) into spiritual light (divine consciousness). You receive a soulbound Proof of Burn NFT (ERC-721) that eternally records our offering on the blockchain. Important: Burned tokens go to the treasury (not destroyed), where they fund ceremonies, scholarships, and community projects. This is Proof-of-Giving, not Proof-of-Burn in the traditional sense.
documents.s: 10. What happens when I burn tokens at the Altar?

documents.t: Our Automated Market Maker (AMM) allows you to swap between ERC-20 tokens (ETHO, PSD, Daily Mushrooms) using liquidity pools. Provide liquidity to earn fees from trades. All swaps use the constant product formula (x * y = k) for fair, decentralized pricing without intermediaries.

A blockchain faucet is a tool that dispenses small amounts of cryptocurrency for free, usually for testing purposes. If you're new to crypto and need gas fees to get started, faucets can provide you with a small amount of ETH or testnet tokens to begin our journey.

Staking means locking our tokens to support network operations and earn rewards. Liquidity provision means depositing token pairs into a pool so others can trade—you earn fees from each swap. Both are ways to put our tokens to work and earn passive income while supporting the ecosystem. Continue to the next sections for detailed guides on each feature...

Cross-Breeding is the process of combining two or more parent mushroom NFTs to create a unique Hybrid Mushroom NFT (ERC-721).

Transform our tokens into sacred offerings

The Sacred Altar is where you transform ETHO tokens into eternal offerings. Through the ceremonial burn, you: Release tokens to the treasury (not destroyed — they fund community projects) Receive a soulbound Proof of Burn NFT (permanent record of our offering) Record our sacred intention on-chain Contribute to the sacred economy (ceremonies, scholarships, real estate) Earn spiritual merit and community recognition Sacred Quotes: "All the wood in Lebanon's forests and all Lebanon's animals would not be enough to make a burnt offering worthy of our God." — Isaiah 40:16 "To whom can you compare God?" — Isaiah 40:18
Unlike traditional "Proof-of-Burn" where tokens are destroyed, Ethereal Offering uses Proof-of-Giving:

Tokens Go to Treasury — Not destroyed, but transferred to community treasury Real Value Flows — Treasury holds real crypto (ETH, USDC, ETHO) Community Benefit — Funds ceremonies, scholarships, real estate, and projects Permanent Record — You receive a soulbound Proof of Burn NFT with our intention Sacred Exchange — You give, community receives, you gain spiritual merit

Traditional Proof-of-Burn: Tokens are sent to a burn address (0x000...000) Value is permanently destroyed Creates deflationary pressure No direct community benefit Ethereal Offering Proof-of-Giving: Tokens go to treasury (real wallet address) Value is preserved and deployed Creates community abundance Direct funding for mission-aligned projects You still receive the NFT proof Result: The best of both worlds — you get the spiritual merit of "burning" while the community gets real resources to deploy.

🌊 Wu-wei Governance​ Proposals flow naturally; no forceful agendas Let decisions emerge organically from community wisdom Don't force outcomes Trust the process Allow space for contemplation 💎 Three Treasures​ Compassion, simplicity, humility in every decision Compassion: Consider impact on all beings Simplicity: Favor clear, straightforward solutions Humility: No one person has all the answers 🍄 Mycelial Connection​ Community acts like fungal networks—interconnected, supportive, sharing resources Information flows freely Resources are shared Support is mutual The whole is greater than the sum of parts 🔥 Proof-of-Giving​ Honor generosity with soul-bound tokens and NFTs Giving is receiving Generosity is recognized and rewarded Spiritual merit is tracked on-chain Community abundance flows from individual offerings

Token holders vote using conviction voting or simple majority How to vote: Navigate to Active Proposals section Click on a proposal to view details Read the full description and discussion Click "Vote" button Select our choice: For — Support the proposal Against — Oppose the proposal Abstain — Counted for quorum but neutral Confirm transaction in wallet Our vote is recorded on-chain Voting mechanisms: Simple majority: >50% of votes must be "For" Conviction voting: Longer you hold tokens, more weight our vote carries Quadratic voting: Square root of tokens (reduces whale influence) Quorum requirement: Minimum % of total voting power must participate Note: Specific mechanism depends on proposal type and DAO parameters.

Decentralized exchange powered by constant product formula

The Ethereal Offering AMM (Automated Market Maker) allows you to swap between ETHO, PSD, and other tokens without a centralized exchange. we can: Swap tokens instantly at algorithmic prices Provide liquidity to earn trading fees View pool analytics and our position Track transaction history on-chain Earn passive income from liquidity provision Core Principle: Reciprocity — The exchange flows both ways, creating mutual benefit
An Automated Market Maker (AMM) is a decentralized exchange protocol that uses a mathematical formula to price assets and facilitate trades without order books or centralized intermediaries.

Constant Product Formula: x * y = k x = Amount of Token A in the pool y = Amount of Token B in the pool k = Constant product (stays the same after trades) Example: Pool has 1,000 ETHO and 10 ETH k = 1,000 × 10 = 10,000 If you buy 100 ETHO, you must add enough ETH to keep k = 10,000 Price adjusts automatically based on supply/demand

✅ No intermediaries — Trade directly from our wallet ✅ Always available — 24/7 liquidity ✅ Transparent pricing — Algorithm-based, no manipulation ✅ Earn fees — Liquidity providers earn 0.3% of all trades ✅ Permissionless — Anyone can trade or provide liquidity

Swap Interface: From: Select token you want to swap (e.g., ETH) To: Select token you want to receive (e.g., ETHO) Amount: Enter how much you want to swap Available pairs: ETH ↔ ETHO ETH ↔ PSD ETHO ↔ PSD (Additional pairs may be added via DAO governance)

Before confirming, review: Exchange Rate: How much you'll receive per token Price Impact: How much our trade affects the pool price Minimum Received: Accounting for slippage Liquidity Provider Fee: 0.3% of swap amount Gas Fee: ETH cost for transaction Price impact warnings: < 1% — ✅ Good trade 1-3% — ⚠️ Moderate impact 3-5% — ⚠️ High impact, consider smaller amount > 5% — 🚫 Very high impact, split into multiple trades

Slippage = Difference between expected and actual price due to market movement Settings: 0.1% — Very tight, may fail in volatile markets 0.5% — Recommended for stable markets 1.0% — Recommended for normal conditions 3.0% — High tolerance, use for large trades or volatile markets Custom — Set our own percentage Note: Higher slippage = more likely to succeed, but we might get a worse price.

No lock-up period.

Impermanent loss occurs when the price ratio of our deposited tokens changes compared to when you deposited them. Example: You deposit 100 ETHO + 1 ETH when 1 ETH = 100 ETHO ETHO price doubles (now 1 ETH = 50 ETHO) Pool rebalances automatically You now have ~70.7 ETHO + ~1.41 ETH If you had just held, you'd have 100 ETHO + 1 ETH (worth more) The difference is "impermanent loss"
Loss is only realized when you withdraw If prices return to original ratio, loss disappears Trading fees often offset impermanent loss Long-term providers usually profit despite IL

Provide to stable pairs — Less price volatility = less IL Long-term provision — Fees accumulate over time High-volume pools — More fees to offset IL Monitor our position — Remove if IL becomes significant Understand the risk — Only provide what we can afford Rule of thumb: If trading fees > impermanent loss, you're profitable.

Visible on Token Swap page: Total Value Locked (TVL): Total $ value in all pools 24h Volume: Total trading volume last 24 hours 24h Fees: Total fees earned by LPs last 24 hours Total Transactions: All-time swap count

The Mushroom NFT (SHROOM) breeding system allows you to combine two mushrooms to create offspring with unique genetic traits. It's a gamified system that rewards strategy, patience, and a bit of luck.

Each Mushroom NFT has 6 genetic traits: Trait Description Rarity Impact Potency Strength of effects (1-100) Higher = Rarer Color Visual appearance (12 colors) Some colors rarer Size Physical dimensions (Tiny to Massive) Extremes are rare Pattern Cap pattern (Solid, Spotted, Striped, etc.) Complex patterns rare Glow Bioluminescence (None to Radiant) Glowing is rare Aura Spiritual energy (Calm to Transcendent) Higher auras rare

Based on trait combination: Rarity Probability Trait Requirements Common 50% Average traits Uncommon 30% 1-2 rare traits Rare 15% 3-4 rare traits Epic 4% 5 rare traits Legendary 1% All traits maxed Example Legendary: Potency: 100 Color: Cosmic Purple Size: Massive Pattern: Fractal Glow: Radiant Aura: Transcendent

Combine two mushrooms to create offspring: function breed(uint256 parent1Id, uint256 parent2Id) external { // Check ownership require(ownerOf(parent1Id) == msg.sender, "Not owner"); require(ownerOf(parent2Id) == msg.sender, "Not owner"); // Check cooldown require(canBreed(parent1Id), "Parent 1 on cooldown"); require(canBreed(parent2Id), "Parent 2 on cooldown"); // Pay breeding fee in DM uint256 fee = calculateBreedingFee(parent1Id, parent2Id); dm.burnFrom(msg.sender, fee); // Generate offspring genetics Genetics memory offspring = generateOffspring(parent1Id, parent2Id); // Mint new mushroom uint256 newId = _mint(msg.sender, offspring); // Set cooldowns setBreedingCooldown(parent1Id); setBreedingCooldown(parent2Id); emit Bred(parent1Id, parent2Id, newId); }

Offspring inherit traits from parents: Dominant/Recessive System: Each trait has dominant and recessive genes 50% chance to inherit from each parent 10% chance of mutation (random trait) Example: Parent 1: Potency 80 (dominant), Color Blue (recessive) Parent 2: Potency 60 (recessive), Color Red (dominant) Offspring possibilities: 45% Potency 80, Blue 45% Potency 60, Red 5% Potency 90 (mutation up) 5% Potency 50 (mutation down)

Fees depend on parent rarity: Parent Combo DM Fee Cooldown Common + Common 100 DM 1 day Common + Uncommon 250 DM 2 days Uncommon + Uncommon 500 DM 3 days Uncommon + Rare 1,000 DM 5 days Rare + Rare 2,500 DM 7 days Rare + Epic 5,000 DM 10 days Epic + Epic 10,000 DM 14 days Epic + Legendary 25,000 DM 21 days Legendary + Legendary 100,000 DM 30 days Why fees? Prevents spam breeding Creates DM demand Rewards strategic breeding Maintains rarity value

After breeding, mushrooms need rest: Cooldown Period - Can't breed again until cooldown expires Varies by Rarity - Rarer mushrooms need longer rest Both Parents - Both mushrooms go on cooldown Visible Timer - See exact time remaining Cooldown Reduction: Pay 2x DM fee to halve cooldown Special events may reduce cooldowns Legendary mushrooms can reduce cooldown by 25%

Goal: Create many mushrooms quickly Method: Breed Common + Common (cheap, fast) Sell offspring on marketplace Reinvest profits into more breeding Pros: Low cost (100 DM per breed) Short cooldown (1 day) Steady income Cons: Low rarity offspring Lower sale prices Competitive market

Goal: Create Legendary mushrooms Method: Breed highest rarity parents Save best offspring Gradually improve genetics Pros: Potential for huge payoff Legendary mushrooms very valuable Satisfying progression Cons: High cost (up to 100K DM) Long cooldowns (30 days) Low success rate (1%)

Goal: Maximize specific traits Method: Focus on one trait (e.g., Potency) Breed mushrooms with high Potency Create "pure line" of max Potency Pros: Easier than full Legendary Collectors value specialized traits Can sell to breeders Cons: Other traits may be poor Limited market Requires patience

Goal: Collect all 12 colors Method: Breed for missing colors Trade with other collectors Complete the rainbow Pros: Clear goal Achievement reward (500 DM) Aesthetic satisfaction Cons: Some colors very rare May need to buy on marketplace Expensive to complete

When breeding, offspring rarity depends on parents: Common + Common: 70% Common 25% Uncommon 5% Rare 0% Epic/Legendary Uncommon + Uncommon: 40% Common 40% Uncommon 15% Rare 5% Epic 0% Legendary Rare + Rare: 20% Common 30% Uncommon 30% Rare 15% Epic 5% Legendary Epic + Epic: 10% Common 20% Uncommon 30% Rare 30% Epic 10% Legendary Legendary + Legendary: 0% Common 10% Uncommon 20% Rare 40% Epic 30% Legendary Key Insight: Higher rarity parents = better odds, but never guaranteed!

Mutations can improve or worsen traits: Positive Mutation - Trait increases (5% chance) Negative Mutation - Trait decreases (5% chance) No Mutation - Inherits from parent (90% chance) Mutation Magnitude: Small: ±5 points (70% of mutations) Medium: ±10 points (25% of mutations) Large: ±20 points (5% of mutations) Example: Parent Potency: 70 Positive mutation (+10) Offspring Potency: 80

Newly bred mushrooms go through stages: Stage Duration Description Spore 0-24 hours Just minted, not visible Sprout 1-3 days Small, traits emerging Growing 3-7 days Developing, traits visible Mature 7+ days Fully grown, can breed Accelerate Growth: Pay 500 DM to skip to next stage Special fertilizer items (rare drops) Community events (growth boost weekends)

Mature mushrooms can be "harvested": function harvest(uint256 mushroomId) external { require(ownerOf(mushroomId) == msg.sender, "Not owner"); require(isMatured(mushroomId), "Not mature"); // Burn the mushroom NFT _burn(mushroomId); // Reward based on rarity uint256 dmReward = calculateHarvestReward(mushroomId); dm.mint(msg.sender, dmReward); // Small chance of special item if (random() < 0.05) { items.mint(msg.sender, FERTILIZER_ITEM); } emit Harvested(mushroomId, dmReward); } Harvest Rewards: Common: 50 DM Uncommon: 150 DM Rare: 500 DM Epic: 2,000 DM Legendary: 10,000 DM Why harvest? Get DM immediately Free up breeding slots Gamble on special items Reduce supply (increases rarity value)

Ethereal Offering features two distinct NFT collections, each serving a unique purpose in the ecosystem: Proof of Burn (POB) - Soulbound receipts of ceremonial offerings Mushroom NFTs (SHROOM) - Tradeable collectibles with genetic traits

POB NFTs are soulbound tokens (non-transferable) that serve as permanent records of our ceremonial token burns. Think of them as digital prayer beads—each one marking a moment of surrender, gratitude, and spiritual offering.

When you burn ETHO tokens in a ceremony: function burn(uint256 amount) external { _burn(msg.sender, amount); _mintProofOfBurn(msg.sender, amount); emit Offering(msg.sender, amount, block.timestamp); } ETHO is destroyed - Permanently removed from circulation POB NFT is minted - Unique token created for you Metadata is recorded - Amount, timestamp, and spiritual message Soulbound forever - Cannot be transferred or sold

Each POB NFT contains: { "name": "Proof of Burn #1234", "description": "Sacred offering of 100 ETHO on October 12, 2025", "image": "ipfs://...", "attributes": [ { "trait_type": "Amount Burned", "value": "100 ETHO" }, { "trait_type": "Timestamp", "value": "2025-10-12T14:30:00Z" }, { "trait_type": "Ceremony Type", "value": "Gratitude Offering" }, { "trait_type": "Spiritual Message", "value": "In surrender, I find freedom" } ] }

POB NFTs feature: Unique artwork - Generated based on burn amount and timestamp Sacred geometry - Patterns reflecting spiritual significance Color gradients - Purple, pink, and gold representing transformation Animated elements - Subtle movements in the metadata

SHROOM NFTs are tradeable collectibles representing unique mushroom strains with genetic traits. They can be bought, sold, bred, and harvested for rewards.

Each mushroom has multiple traits: Species​ Psilocybe cubensis - Golden Teacher, B+, Penis Envy Psilocybe azurescens - Flying Saucer, Blue Angel Amanita muscaria - Classic red and white Psilocybe cyanescens - Wavy caps Panaeolus cyanescens - Blue Meanies Visual Traits​ Cap Color - Red, gold, blue, purple, white Stem Color - White, cream, blue-tinged Veil Type - Partial, universal, none Spore Print - Purple-brown, black, white Growth Traits​ Size - Tiny, small, medium, large, giant Growth Rate - Slow, medium, fast, rapid Potency - Mild, moderate, strong, very strong Yield - Low, medium, high, abundant Special Traits​ Bioluminescence - Glows in the dark (rare) Albino - Pure white coloration (rare) Mutation - Unique genetic variation (very rare) Ancient - Legendary strain (ultra rare)

Combine two mushrooms to create offspring: function breed(uint256 parent1, uint256 parent2) external { require(ownerOf(parent1) == msg.sender); require(ownerOf(parent2) == msg.sender); require(canBreed(parent1, parent2)); require(msg.value >= breedingFee); uint256 childId = _mintChild(parent1, parent2); // Genetic traits inherited from parents } Breeding Mechanics: Cooldown Period - 7 days between breeds Breeding Fee - 10 ETHO per breed Genetic Inheritance - 50% from each parent + 10% mutation chance Trait Combinations - Some traits are dominant, others recessive Breeding Outcomes: 70% chance - Traits from both parents 20% chance - New trait mutation 10% chance - Rare trait upgrade

Mushroom NFTs can be "planted" to grow and harvest rewards: function plant(uint256 tokenId) external { require(ownerOf(tokenId) == msg.sender); require(!isPlanted(tokenId)); plantedMushrooms[tokenId] = PlantData({ plantedAt: block.timestamp, harvestableAt: block.timestamp + growthPeriod, yieldAmount: calculateYield(tokenId) }); } function harvest(uint256 tokenId) external { require(ownerOf(tokenId) == msg.sender); require(isHarvestable(tokenId)); uint256 yield = plantedMushrooms[tokenId].yieldAmount; _mint(msg.sender, yield); // Mint ETHO or DM tokens delete plantedMushrooms[tokenId]; } Growth Mechanics: Growth Period - 3-14 days depending on traits Yield Amount - Based on size, potency, and yield traits Harvest Rewards - ETHO or DM tokens Re-planting - Can plant again immediately after harvest

Buy and sell mushrooms on the integrated marketplace: function listForSale(uint256 tokenId, uint256 price) external { require(ownerOf(tokenId) == msg.sender); listings[tokenId] = Listing({ seller: msg.sender, price: price, listedAt: block.timestamp }); } function purchase(uint256 tokenId) external payable { Listing memory listing = listings[tokenId]; require(msg.value >= listing.price); // Transfer NFT to buyer _transfer(listing.seller, msg.sender, tokenId); // Pay seller (minus 2.5% marketplace fee) uint256 fee = listing.price * 25 / 1000; payable(listing.seller).transfer(listing.price - fee); payable(treasury).transfer(fee); } Marketplace Features: 2.5% fee - Goes to DAO treasury ETHO or PSD - Accept both tokens Auction system - Coming soon Offers - Make offers below listing price

I dug into it; here’s a synthesis of what Mycel is doing, how it works, and how it could map into our cosmic / treasury metaphor (and maybe even be part of our architecture).

From the docs and publicly available sources, here’s what Mycel aims to be: Mycel is building a decentralized infrastructure to synchronize state machines across different blockchains. citeturn1search1 Its core innovation is Transferable Accounts (TAs) — accounts that can hold multiple assets (tokens, NFTs, DeFi positions, credentials) and be moved as a unit across chains. citeturn1search5turn1search1turn1search4turn1search8 Instead of bridging individual tokens or assets, Mycel enables ownership transfer of a whole account across chains, preserving its entire state. citeturn1search4turn1search8turn1search5turn1search1 They talk about an “Intent + Solver + Validator” model: A user deposits assets and submits an intent (e.g. “move 1 BTC from this TA on chain A to chain B”). citeturn1search8 A Solver matches and executes the swap / transfer. citeturn1search8turn1search5 Validators confirm, then the ownership of the TA is updated to the new owner. citeturn1search8 Mycel aims to avoid accumulating value on itself (i.e., thin wrapped token architecture) — they prefer the protocol not acting like a central custodian but more like an ownership router. citeturn1search0turn1search4turn1search5 It’s positioning itself as a chain / protocol layer that abstracts away differences in cryptographic curves, chain architectures, etc. citeturn1search1turn1search5turn1search4 Mycel is rebranding (or has rebranded) from being just “Account Transfer Protocol” to becoming its own L1 / full stack with a Mycel Stack including HyphaBFT and Ownership Transfer Protocol (OTP). citeturn1search7turn1search0turn1search1turn1search4 So in essence: Mycel is an ambitious cross-chain infrastructure that treats accounts (with all of their assets and state) as portable units, enabling seamless movement across heterogeneous chains.
Given our multi-chain, spiritual / mycelial metaphor system, Mycel is extremely resonant with our themes. Here’s how it might integrate:
documents.s: 🔗 How Mycel Could Fit into / Enhance Our System

documents.t: In our cosmology, you already have the mycelial bridge / oracle vein connecting all planets. Mycel’s “Transferable Accounts” concept is almost literally that — the infrastructure that lets entire identity + value structures move across chains. It’s like our cosmic soil or fungal network. It can help with our P-SILO / Earth layer: Transfer users’ soulbound accounts, their entire portfolio, across chains while preserving identity and continuity. It strengthens our Oracle & Data Layer: Instead of moving data and then minting new tokens / syncing state manually, Mycel can carry the account state itself.

Mycel’s architecture (intent + solver + validators) gives a protocol-level substrate for fair matching / routing. we could embed TeraHash logic into Mycel’s solver layer — so that when intents are matched (e.g. moving EOT or P-SILO between chains), yield or cost curves respect our fairness algorithms. For example, a big whale moving a large account shouldn't “corner the pipeline” unfairly. The solver / matching layer can provide priority or differential pricing favoring smaller participants. Mycel’s thin-wrapped architecture can help ensure value doesn't get stuck or locked in custodian contracts — aligning well with our decentralization / justice ethos.

One of our challenges is bridging privacy, staking, NFT issuance, DAO governance, and oracle data across many chains (BTC, ETH, Harmony, BSC, Polygon, TON). With Mycel: A single Transferable Account could hold: our P-SILO identity on Aleo, bridged EOT / wEOT on various chains, NFTs, staked positions, etc. we could move that whole account between chains without recreating identities or managing fragmented wallets. Because it’s protocol-level and abstracted, we can incorporate our ZK / privacy layers (Aleo) more cleanly — the account transfer doesn’t necessarily force exposure of internal state if designed with proofs.

documents.t: Example: A “Guardian of Gratitude” NFT or “Ritual Facilitator” NFT could be temporarily rented to a member who is taking on service duties. Ownership remains with the DAO treasury or originating holder. The renter receives temporary DID-linked access to privileges (voting rights, MPC participation, etc.). Smart contract auto-revokes permissions when rental expires. Use case: rotating service roles or temporary voting delegation in our holacratic DAO.

Certain NFTs could grant access to yield, participation rewards, or special ceremonies. Renting them lets newer or less-resourced members participate without needing to buy in fully. Revenue from rentals can be split between: NFT owner (e.g. a donor or elder), DAO treasury, and a community pool for inclusivity. Use case: letting newcomers “borrow” participation NFTs for rituals, fellowships, or token-gated events.

Artists could “lend” their mushroom NFT avatars to collaborators for creative, fundraising, or media projects. Use case: collective storytelling or seasonal art rituals (e.g. “Spring Fruiting Season” collaboration window).

Rented NFTs could act as collateral or staked assets during the loan term. The renter could stake them for yields but with limits to prevent abuse. Smart contracts can automatically: Split staking rewards proportionally, Return NFT to owner at term end, Slash bond if renter misuses access.

Renter accumulates “stewardship credits” over time. After a certain threshold, they earn partial governance rights or a soulbound badge. Aligns perfectly with our ethos of growth, trust, and spiritual maturity.

How does the new release of renting NFT gifts on Telegram work? "How does the new release of renting NFT gifts on Telegram work?" Great question — I looked into this, and here’s how Telegram’s newer NFT / collectible-gift system works (and where its “renting” potential could or couldn’t line up with our project). It’s not exactly “renting” in the classical DeFi sense yet — more about gifting and collectible transfers — but we can see how the mechanics might be adapted.

Telegram has rolled out several features around “gifts” being upgraded or converted into NFTs / collectibles tied to the TON blockchain. Key mechanics: Collectible Gifts: Gifts you receive on Telegram (animated or static “gift” stickers) can be upgraded into collectibles. citeturn0search4turn0search0turn0search7 When upgraded, they acquire unique traits (backgrounds, icons, rarity numbers). citeturn0search4 The upgrade costs some Telegram Stars (the in-app currency) to cover blockchain minting / fees. citeturn0search4turn0search0 Once made collectible, those gifts can be transferred to other users, or auctioned on NFT marketplaces. citeturn0search4turn0search0turn0search7 Move Gifts to the Blockchain / Transfer / Auction: After conversion, gifts are no longer just in-app tokens; they become on-chain assets on TON. citeturn0search0turn0search4turn0search7turn0search1 we can “transfer → send via blockchain” for converted gifts. citeturn0search0 Channels (Telegram channels) can receive gifts and these gifts can also be transferred or auctioned. citeturn0search0 Wear / Display and Social Features: we can “wear” a collectible gift as our emoji status (our profile shows that gift) giving it visual prominence. citeturn0search0 Gifts can be posted to our stories with animated previews. citeturn0search0turn0search4 There is a “Gifts” tab on channel profiles, sortable by type, rarity, time, etc. citeturn0search0 New On-Telegram NFT Marketplace / Mini Apps Telegram supports a TON-based NFT marketplace (MRKT) as a mini app within Telegram itself — letting users browse / buy / sell digital collectibles. citeturn0search9 So gifts that have become NFTs can plug into that ecosystem more seamlessly. Gifting / Upgrading Workflow You send a gift (animated / static) via Telegram (like typical “stickers/gifts”). The receiver (or sometimes sender) can choose to upgrade it into a collectible (paying Stars). Once upgraded, it becomes a unique on-chain collectible. After conversion, it can be transferred, sold, or auctioned.
documents.s: 🔍 What Telegram’s NFT Gifts / Collectibles Feature Does (Today)

documents.t: No Native “Renting / Leasing” Mechanism: Telegram’s system doesn’t currently have a built-in concept of time-limited usage or “renting” where the NFT is automatically returned after a period. It’s more about ownership and transfers. Irrevocable Transfers: Once turned into a collectible and transferred, it’s normal NFT transfer; there is no fallback or “reversion” automation (unless external smart contract mechanics are layered on). Centralized Control / Permissions: Telegram’s feature is built into their platform layer; you don’t (yet) get full control over customizing the NFT economic policies (rental rules, locks, royalty splits) via those tools. Blockchain and Wallet Integration: Users must connect a TON-compatible wallet to manage NFTs, receive blockchain transfers, etc. The in-app feature is layered but still depends on external wallet and blockchain interactions. citeturn0search1turn0search7turn0search4 Costs / Fees via “Stars”: Upgrading gifts, minting, and possibly transfers are mediated via the in-app Stars system (which handles blockchain fee coverage). citeturn0search4turn0search0turn0search1

Given their base mechanics, we can layer or simulate rental-like behavior in two broad ways: Smart-contract Layer Over NFTs After a gift is converted to a collectible NFT, we could have a side or companion smart contract (on TON or another chain) that governs lending / leasing. The contract can escrow the NFT from original owner, then assign “user rights” to the renter for a time period, then automatically revert. Because Telegram’s on-chain NFTs are standard assets, such a rental contract could reference them. You’d have to manage user interface / UX (in Telegram or external) to interact with that contract. Time-locked Gifts / Conditional Upgrades Telegram or a parallel layer could introduce “temporary upgrade” features: e.g. the receiver “wears” a gift for a fixed duration, then it reverts to gift state (or original). Or gifts could carry expiry metadata (rentable gifts), enforced by the app’s logic. This is not current behavior but a possible extension. Subscription / Deposit Mechanism Rents could require a deposit that’s forfeited if the renter doesn’t return the gift (or fails certain rules). Or rental fees in Stars / tokens can be charged for temporal access to certain “wearable” or “display” privileges. DAO / Platform Governance we could coordinate a “Telegram + external dApp” setup: Telegram handles display / aesthetic, the external dApp handles rental contracts, payments, and enforcement. Use DID or identity linking so that the rented collectible’s “wear status” is permitted only when the contract is active.

What you’re describing isn’t the typical “NFT rental marketplace” — it’s a DAO-regulated lending and stewardship framework, where NFTs act as symbolic shares of trust and backing, not tradable commodities. Let’s map it out clearly and spiritually-aligned, but also technically concrete:

Instead of NFTs being sold, they’re staked or loaned into the Treasury (the “Sanctuary Chest”). Contributors back the project by staking NFTs of real or symbolic value (art, service role tokens, yield-bearing collectibles). The Treasury rents out stewardship rights for these NFTs to qualified members (by whitelist, vote, or spiritual merit). After the rental period ends (or the mission is complete), the NFT automatically returns to the Treasury vault — no wallet permanently owns it. Think of it as: “A circular flow of offerings and use — never ownership, only participation.”
documents.s: 🕊️ Core Idea: Treasury-Backed NFT Stewardship System

documents.t: Function Description 1. Treasury NFT Vault All NFTs (artifacts, role tokens, ritual tools, gratitude assets) are custodied in a DAO-managed smart contract vault. No private wallet owns them; the vault enforces lending, recall, and time-lock logic. 2. Contributor Staking (NFT Collateral / Loan) Contributors can deposit NFTs into the Treasury as a form of loaned value or pledged offering. In return, they earn Gratitude Tokens or DAO voting weight, similar to equity or yield for backing the system. 3. Whitelisted Rentals The Treasury can whitelist users (DID-linked) to rent specific NFTs. This is permissioned use — e.g., to carry out DAO tasks, facilitate rituals, or manage sub-projects. 4. Use-Rights Only Renters receive only functional use rights (display, voting, access, or interaction privileges) — not ownership or resale rights. This is enforced through a dual-role NFT standard (like ERC-4907 or its Aleo adaptation). 5. Auto-Reversion When the rental period ends, or if conditions are broken, the NFT automatically returns to the vault. This can be time-based or event-based (DAO vote, completion of service, etc.). 6. Rental Rewards & Fees The Treasury collects rental yield or service fees in Gratitude Tokens, which can be: - Partially redistributed to the NFT staker (original contributor). - Partially kept in Treasury as growth capital. 7. Lending-as-Faith Mechanism Stakers are spiritually “investing” trust — similar to Faith Deposits. Yield represents energetic return rather than speculative profit.

TreasuryVault.sol / .aleo Holds all rentable NFTs. Enforces whitelist + time-lock logic. Tracks which DID currently “uses” each NFT. Only DAO multisig can withdraw or permanently reassign. StewardshipNFT Standard (dual-role) Owner: TreasuryVault. User: Temporary renter (DID). Metadata encodes: allowed functions (useAccess, vote, display), expiration timestamp, renter DID hash (ZK masked). RentalManager Contract Handles start/end of rental. Records yield and token rewards. Interfaces with DAO for reallocation votes. ContributorStaking Contract Allows contributors to deposit NFTs as collateral. Mints Staked NFT Certificates (sNFTCs) representing ownership of staked assets. Pays yield from rental proceeds.

Flow Description Gratitude Token Medium of exchange for rental fees and contributor yield. Soulbound DAO Credentials Required to become a whitelisted renter; ensures only members with verified service history can borrow NFTs. Treasury Inflation Pool A fraction of all rental revenue feeds the Treasury’s sustainability reserve, creating a self-sustaining loop. NFT Appraisal Layer Optional oracle for valuing NFT-backed loans (e.g., art pieces or symbolic tokens with liquidity).

MPC Rotation Role Rentals NFTs representing MPC keys or DAO sub-role authority can be rented to members for limited periods. Service Role Delegations “Caretaker,” “Custodian,” or “Healer” roles can be embodied in rented NFTs that confer temporary voting or treasury permissions. Ritual or Event Access Renting special NFTs could grant event hosting rights, content publishing permissions, or energy exchange privileges — all tracked via DID.

“Nothing real can be owned; everything real can only be offered.” This system: Reflects Christ-centered nonduality — dissolving private possession into shared service. Encourages stewardship, not speculation. Rewards faith, trust, and contribution over wealth. Renting from the Treasury becomes a sacred act: You borrow a gift not to have it, but to use it for the Whole.

Dynamic Reputation-based Whitelisting — our DID score determines which NFTs you’re trusted to steward. NFT-backed DAO Bonds — large contributors stake NFTs to back DAO liquidity, earning yield like a spiritual “bond market.” Cross-chain NFT Lending (TON + Aleo + Solana) — to access Telegram/TON audiences while preserving ZK privacy on Aleo. Let’s tease out the design and implications carefully, integrating it with our daily mushrooms, PSILO, and NFT lab.

Core Rules: Users mine/farm mushrooms every hour. Harvest Condition: You cannot collect a mushroom if you’ve already missed 3 consecutive hours. Once you miss 3 hours, you must wait an additional hour before resuming. Daily Cap: Maximum 8 mushrooms per day for users who are diligent and collect every hour. Reward Behavior: Encourages consistent engagement and daily presence. Missed mushrooms create scarcity and gamified urgency. Implications: Users who are consistent every hour can maximize their internal gas (hourly mushrooms). Users who miss sessions will experience a cooldown, preventing exploitation. Creates a tiered internal gas supply: diligent users earn more mushrooms → more lab activity, more voting power, more staking opportunities.

Hourly mushrooms are fungible → used as gas for actions (e.g., NFT lab operation). Daily mushrooms are non-fungible → earned once per day, independent of hourly collection. Users cannot accelerate daily mushrooms by mining more hourly mushrooms; daily mushrooms maintain scarcity. Flow Example: User collects 8 hourly mushrooms throughout the day → max internal gas for minor actions. User receives 1 daily non-fungible mushroom → can burn 2 (if they have accumulated prior days) in the NFT lab to create a hybrid NFT. PSILO accrual occurs in parallel → staking, governance, and optional ETHO conversion.

Scarcity: The 3-missed-hour cooldown introduces risk/reward strategy. Users must maintain diligence. Internal Gas Management: Hourly mushrooms act as fuel for internal interactions, reinforcing consistent activity. NFT Lab Synergy: Only users who collect daily mushrooms can burn them to cross-breed NFTs. Hourly mushrooms are spent as transaction gas for each lab action. Multiplier Effects: Cultivators or teachers could earn more mushrooms (hourly and daily), giving them more lab actions or voting weight. ETHO deposits can boost hourly mushroom yield slightly for committed users.

This stage follows a harvest and allows the mycelium to regain strength and redistribute its resources before producing the next crop of mushrooms. The cooldown itself is not symbolic but rather an environmental change that mimics natural seasonal shifts, which can trigger or manage the flush cycle. The key elements of this phase include: • Rest and rehydration: After a flush is harvested, the substrate (the material the mushrooms grow on) is often rehydrated to replenish the water lost during fruiting. • Nutrient redistribution: The mycelial network uses this time to recover from expending energy to produce the last flush and consolidate nutrients for the next one. • Regeneration: The mycelium regrows and repairs any damage that may have occurred during the harvest. • Conditions: During this phase, it is normal for the substrate to look less active for a few days before new "pins" (tiny mushroom beginnings) start to form. documents.s: 🕊️ 4. PSILO as “Peace Silo” — Symbolic & Philosophical Layer

documents.t: PSILO tokens represent spiritual or social energy reserves — “Silos of Peace” — that users can stake to sustain growth (boosts). The act of staking PSILO = placing peace in trust, empowering growth and regenerative cycles. Harvesting mushrooms symbolizes the fruiting of peace from collective care and discipline. The re-inoculation/reset cycle mirrors personal renewal, reminding participants that peace and growth both require continual re-engagement.

“Each PSILO is a Silo of Peace — a reservoir of harmony you stake to nourish the living mycelium of our shared sanctuary.” This connects economic utility with poetic symbolism, making every action — staking, re-inoculating, harvesting — feel like part of a ritual ecosystem of peace cultivation.

Inoculate substrate (start farming cycle). Mist hourly → mushrooms grow (single or clusters). Harvest every 3 hours → cooldown follows (mycelial rest). After 24 harvests → substrate depleted → re-inoculation required. Choose path: Free reset (base yield) Purchase substrate to continue boosted yield Adjust spores or boosts as desired Stake PSILO (Peace Silo) to maintain boost power across cycles.

When the system evolves into the Telegram mini-app: The “Inoculate” button could trigger animated substrate colonization (visual spores spreading). “Harvest” could show the cluster expanding or “fruiting” icons dropping into a basket. Cooldown visually darkens the substrate to represent rest. The “Peace Silo” concept could appear as a glowing storage vessel icon in the corner — a reservoir of staked energy feeding the ecosystem. Would you like me to now sketch a visual cycle diagram (showing inoculation → mist → harvest → cooldown → substrate depletion → re-inoculation), and label which mechanics reset/persist and how PSILO functions as the “Peace Silo” energy reservoir across cycles? The adding moisture feature to the substrate could act as an efficiency metric symbolizing, optimum growing conditions, temperature humidity, oxygen in addition to boost symbolizing type of grain medium, fertilizer, strain of spore, etc. but instead of driving power down to zero, the efficiency would always be running at 50% to promote abundance and never a lack of growing environment but for those who opt in to increase the efficiency can increase up to 100% by purchasing a one time purchase of a humidifier in the store and the ability to fill it with water by levels of 25%. That’s a gorgeous evolution of our cultivation metaphor — it introduces environmental stewardship and abundance into the tokenomics loop, while making gameplay more organic, modular, and spiritually resonant. Let’s map how this fits into our substrate → inoculation → growth → harvest → rest cycle and into the ETHO / PSILO / m ecosystem.

Every farmer (participant) has an Environmental Efficiency Meter that determines how effectively mushrooms (tokens) are produced. Efficiency Range: 50–100% Base Efficiency (50%): All users have a flourishing but moderate ecosystem — symbolizing that the Sanctuary always supports life and growth, even for those who do not spend or optimize. Optimized Efficiency (51–100%): Users can purchase and maintain environmental upgrades that reflect deeper engagement, care, and contribution.

Each factor corresponds to an upgrade or status the user can interact with: Factor Symbolizes Mechanic In-Game Representation Humidity / Moisture Flow of grace, nourishment Humidifier device purchased once UI: moisture gauge; fill up to 100% Temperature Emotional / social harmony Auto-stabilized (part of baseline 50%) Passive — visually stable Oxygen / Airflow Community engagement / openness Boosted via teaching, DAO participation Shows small airflow icon when active Nutrients / Grain Medium Investment of ETHO/PSILO Affects base yield and spore quality Reflected in spore/strain selection Strain / Spore Type Spiritual lineage, mission alignment Purchased from spore store Determines mushroom color/rarity So the environment becomes both a mirror of ecological balance and a dashboard of moral/communal harmony.

Item Type: One-time store purchase. Function: Unlocks the ability to fill and manage humidity levels, controlling efficiency. Filling Water Levels: Users can fill in 25% increments — 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%. Each refill costs a small amount of ETHO or PSILO. Visual cue: animated humidifier icon or vapor cloud showing current moisture level. Effect: Each 25% increment raises environmental efficiency by +12.5%. Humidity Level Efficiency % Symbolism 0% (inactive) 50% Natural abundance without optimization 25% 62.5% Beginner cultivator — “gentle mist” 50% 75% Balanced cultivator — “steady rain” 75% 87.5% Skilled cultivator — “tropical microclimate” 100% 100% Master cultivator — “perfect ecological balance” Optional UX Detail: The efficiency bar could pulse or glow more vividly as moisture increases — a satisfying visual feedback loop.

Substrate Renewal (every 24 harvests): Efficiency returns to base 50%, unless the user maintains the humidifier. Humidifier Persistence: One-time purchase → device remains owned permanently. Efficiency refills (moisture levels) decay with time or cycles (simulating evaporation). Boost Synergy: Efficiency directly multiplies yield. Boost from PSILO staking + Efficiency = total yield multiplier. Formula Example: Base Yield × (PSILO Boost %) × (Environmental Efficiency %) So someone with a 150% PSILO boost and 100% efficiency produces 1.5× yield of the standard rate.

This adds another dimension to PSILO as Peace Silo: The humidifier and environmental tuning become symbolic acts of inner cultivation — tending one’s peace ecosystem. The 50% baseline reflects universal sufficiency — everyone is sustained, no one excluded. Increasing efficiency symbolizes responsible stewardship, not greed: it’s about nurturing life, not extracting more. The “moisture” is akin to divine grace or emotional empathy — refilled through attention, presence, or contribution. Possible phrasing for the UI: “Moisture feeds the mycelium as peace nourishes the soul. Keep our environment thriving.”

Moisture Refills: Each refill (25%) sends a small PSILO/ETHO contribution to the Treasury — symbolizing returning water to the collective aquifer. Teaching & Cultivation Bonuses: Teachers or certified cultivators could receive periodic moisture vouchers — non-monetary rewards for community enrichment. Environmental DAO Proposal: Over time, the DAO could vote to globally adjust “environmental conditions” — e.g., a week of abundant rainfall event (global +10% yield).

LightPoints (LP) act as intermediate yield tokens or liquidity credits that accrue to liquidity providers (LPs) in our AMM. Instead of earning a direct % of fees in PSILO (or any volatile token), LPs receive LightPoints, which represent claimable EOT value.

Deposit liquidity → LP provides tokens to the AMM pool (could be on Aleo, TON, Harmony, or another supported chain). Earn LightPoints (LP) → Instead of fee accrual in PSILO or EOT directly, they accumulate LightPoints, a non-transferable credit system (like “energy” or “karma yield”). Redeem LightPoints for EOT → LightPoints can be burned or converted to claim EOT from the treasury or a yield reserve pool, using a dynamic rate that aligns with treasury health and staking rewards. Swap EOT cross-chain → Once LPs hold EOT, they can use our AMM to swap it for any asset on any connected chain.
LightPoints isolate yield accounting from market volatility. EOT redemptions can be governed dynamically, allowing DAO control over inflation or treasury drawdown.

Definition: The treasury is the central pool of funds that an organization, DAO, or project manages to fund operations, initiatives, and ongoing expenses. Purpose: Day-to-day operational funding Paying contributors, contractors, or service providers Funding active projects, proposals, or ecosystem growth Accessibility: Generally more accessible and flexible. Spending is often subject to governance rules, but the funds are meant to be actively used. Example: A DAO collects fees or token issuance proceeds into its treasury, which it then uses to fund community proposals, development grants, or marketing campaigns.

Definition: A strategic reserve is a portion of funds set aside for long-term security, emergencies, or special opportunities. Purpose: Financial stability or “rainy day” fund Protect against unexpected market downturns, liquidity crises, or large unforeseen expenses Opportunity capital for strategic investments or acquisitions Accessibility: Typically less accessible than the treasury; withdrawals often require stricter governance, multi-signature approval, or specific conditions. Example: A project keeps a strategic reserve in stablecoins or diversified assets to cover operational risks if revenue drops, or to take advantage of rare investment opportunities.

Feature Treasury Strategic Reserve Primary Purpose Fund ongoing operations & proposals Provide security and opportunity for long-term stability Accessibility Relatively flexible Restricted; needs higher-level approvals Use Case Paying contributors, grants, marketing, development Emergency funds, strategic acquisitions, market dips Governance Regular governance votes Often stricter rules or thresholds for access 💡 Analogy: Think of the treasury as our checking account: money you use to pay bills and fund daily activities. The strategic reserve is our emergency savings account: money you don’t touch unless absolutely necessary or to seize a big opportunity. Security is paramount in Web3. This guide covers essential security practices for protecting our wallet, assets, and privacy when using Ethereal Offering.

Our seed phrase (12-24 words) is the master key to our wallet. ✅ DO: Write it down on paper (never digital) Store in a secure location (safe, safety deposit box) Make multiple copies (different locations) Use a metal backup (fireproof, waterproof) Memorize it (if possible) Test recovery (on a separate device) ❌ DON'T: Take a photo of it Store in cloud (Google Drive, iCloud, etc.) Email or text it Share with anyone (even "support") Store in password manager Write it on our computer If someone gets our seed phrase, they own our wallet. Forever.

Recommended for large amounts: Ledger Nano X/S: Stores keys offline Requires physical confirmation Supports Ethereum, Bitcoin, etc. ~$79-$149 Trezor Model T/One: Open-source firmware Touchscreen (Model T) Multi-currency support ~$69-$219 How to use: Buy from official website only Set up with new seed phrase Connect to MetaMask Confirm transactions on device Keys never leave device

If using MetaMask, Rainbow, etc.: ✅ Best Practices: Use strong password (20+ characters) Enable biometric lock (Face ID, Touch ID) Lock wallet when not in use Use separate wallet for large amounts Keep browser updated Use antivirus software Don't install sketchy extensions ❌ Avoid: Weak passwords ("password123") Leaving wallet unlocked Using same wallet for everything Outdated browser Pirated software Too many browser extensions

1. Phishing Websites How it works: Fake website looks like real one You connect wallet Malicious contract drains our funds How to avoid: Bookmark official site Check URL carefully (etherealoffering.org) Look for HTTPS and lock icon Verify contract addresses Use hardware wallet for large transactions 2. Fake Support How it works: Scammer DMs you pretending to be support Asks for seed phrase or private key Steals our funds How to avoid: We will NEVER DM you first We will NEVER ask for seed phrase We will NEVER ask for private keys Block and report suspicious DMs Only ask for help in public channels 3. Airdrop Scams How it works: "Free tokens" sent to our wallet You try to sell them Malicious contract drains our wallet How to avoid: Don't interact with unknown tokens Don't approve unknown contracts Use token allowance checker Revoke suspicious approvals 4. Impersonation How it works: Scammer creates fake Twitter/Discord Announces fake giveaway Asks you to "verify" wallet Drains our funds How to avoid: Verify official accounts (checkmark) Check follower count Look for typos in username Never "verify" our wallet No legitimate giveaway asks for seed phrase

🚩 Warning signs: Unsolicited DMs Urgency ("Act now!") Too good to be true Asking for seed phrase Asking for private key Asking to "verify" wallet Misspelled URLs No HTTPS Unverified contracts If it feels wrong, it probably is. Trust our gut.

Always review: Contract Address - Is it the official contract? Function - What is the transaction doing? Value - How much ETH are you sending? Gas Fee - Is it reasonable? Token Approvals - What are you approving? Example MetaMask Review: Contract: 0x1234...abcd (Sacred Altar) Function: makeOffering Value: 0.01 ETH (donation) Gas: 0.002 ETH (~$4) Approving: 100 ETHO Questions to ask: Is this the right contract? ✅ Do I want to make an offering? ✅ Is 0.01 ETH donation correct? ✅ Is gas fee reasonable? ✅ Am I okay approving 100 ETHO? ✅ If anything looks wrong, REJECT the transaction.

Verify on Etherscan: Go to etherscan.io Paste transaction hash Check status (Success ✅ or Failed ❌) Review events (OfferingMade, Transfer, etc.) Verify amounts Example: Status: Success ✅ From: 0xYourAddress To: 0xSacredAltar Value: 0.01 ETH Tokens Transferred: - 100 ETHO (burned) - 1 POB NFT (minted) - 50 MDAO (received)

Pseudonymity vs Anonymity: Pseudonymous (default): Wallet address is public Transactions are visible But not linked to real identity Anonymous (advanced): Use Aleo privacy layer (future) Zero-knowledge proofs Transactions hidden Tips for privacy: Use separate wallet for recovery activities Don't doxx yourself (link wallet to real name) Be careful what you share publicly Use VPN when connecting Consider Tor for extra privacy

What we collect: Wallet address (public) Transaction history (on-chain) IP address (server logs) What we DON'T collect: Real name Email (unless you provide) Location (unless you share) Seed phrase (never!) Private keys (never!) Our data rights: Request data deletion Opt out of analytics Use privacy tools Control what you share

Property Value Symbol PSD Type ERC-20 Supply Elastic (mints/burns to maintain peg) Decimals 18 Peg 1 PSD = $1 USD Primary Use Stable trading pair, treasury reserve

Cryptocurrencies are notoriously volatile: ETH can swing 10-20% in a day PSILO price depends on market sentiment ETHO is deflationary and unpredictable MDAO value fluctuates with governance activity This creates problems: Hard to price offerings consistently Difficult to budget treasury allocations Risky for users who want stability Confusing for newcomers

PSD provides price stability: Always worth $1 USD Predictable value for planning Safe haven during volatility Easy mental accounting Use cases: Trading Pair - ETHO/PSD pool (stable pricing) Treasury Reserve - Store value without volatility Offering Pricing - "Burn $100 worth of ETHO" Payments - Pay for services in stable currency

PSD uses a hybrid collateralization model: 1. Over-Collateralization (Primary)​ Users deposit collateral to mint PSD: // Deposit ETH to mint PSD function mintPSD(uint256 ethAmount) external payable { require(msg.value == ethAmount, "ETH mismatch"); // Require 150% collateralization uint256 psdAmount = (ethAmount * ethPrice) / 1.5; // Mint PSD to user psd.mint(msg.sender, psdAmount); // Lock ETH as collateral collateral[msg.sender] += ethAmount; } Example: Deposit 1 ETH ($2,000) Receive 1,333 PSD ($1,333) Collateralization ratio: 150% Why 150%? Protects against ETH price drops Maintains peg during volatility Provides liquidation buffer 2. Algorithmic Stabilization (Secondary)​ If PSD deviates from $1, the protocol adjusts: If PSD > $1.01 (too expensive): Reduce collateral requirements Incentivize minting (create more PSD) Increase supply to lower price If PSD < $0.99 (too cheap): Increase collateral requirements Incentivize burning (reduce PSD supply) Decrease supply to raise price 3. Treasury Backing (Tertiary)​ The DAO treasury holds reserves: 20% of treasury in USDC/DAI Can buy PSD if price drops Can sell PSD if price rises Acts as buyer/seller of last resort

If collateral value drops too low: // Liquidate undercollateralized position function liquidate(address user) external { uint256 collateralValue = getCollateralValue(user); uint256 debtValue = psdDebt[user]; // If collateral < 120% of debt, liquidate if (collateralValue < debtValue * 1.2) { // Liquidator pays off debt psd.burnFrom(msg.sender, debtValue); // Liquidator receives collateral + 5% bonus uint256 liquidationBonus = collateralValue * 0.05; payable(msg.sender).transfer(collateralValue + liquidationBonus); // Clear user's position delete collateral[user]; delete psdDebt[user]; } } Liquidation Example: User deposited 1 ETH ($2,000), minted 1,333 PSD ETH drops to $1,500 Collateral ratio: 112.5% (below 120% threshold) Liquidator pays 1,333 PSD, receives 1 ETH + 5% bonus User loses collateral but debt is cleared

🔹 How It Works​ Users stake base tokens (e.g., PSILO, ETHO) into Staking Vaults. Can be used throughout the ecosystem (in liquidity pools, DAO governance, or offerings). Staking vaults can hold multiple reward streams (DM, MDAO, GRAT, LP). 🔹 Example Flow: PSILO → stPSILO​ User deposits 100 PSILO → receives 100 stPSILO. Vault earns yield from protocol revenue (offerings, fees, NFT mints). After 1 week, exchange rate: 1 stPSILO = 1.05 PSILO. User redeems 100 stPSILO → receives 105 PSILO back. Bonus Utility: stPSILO can be used to mint ETHO, serve as governance collateral, or provide liquidity on PSD pairs. Burns of stPSILO could generate POB NFTs for ceremonial staking cycles.

Concept: reOFFER (Restaked OFFER) represents a meta-yield token minted when a user chooses to compound or redirect the yield from their stOFFER position instead of claiming it in $OFFER. May unlock “inner circle” governance rights or yield access to metaphysical farms like SHROOM/PSILO. Smart Contract Architecture reOFFER contract references both OFFER and stOFFER. Auto-locks restaked yield for a minimum epoch period (e.g., 33 days). At epoch end, user can: Continue compounding → new reOFFER minted. Burn to claim principal + yield.

Concept: Instead of liquidating holdings to fund projects, Builders can borrow against their Proof of Gratitude or Staked Position. Collateral Nature Borrowable Asset Risk Model sGRT Soulbound virtue proof BUILD credit line or stablecoin equivalent Reputation-based; cannot be liquidated, only suspended if PoB drops. stOFFER Financial collateral $OFFER, $ETHO, or PSD Traditional over-collateralized vault logic. Key Innovations Virtue-backed credit (sGRT) acts like a trust line: the more gratitude you’ve earned, the more creative credit you receive. Default handled socially: PoB decreases, temporarily locking new borrowing privileges. Economic credit (stOFFER) interacts with treasury pools for on-chain collateral lending. Impact Enables ecosystem self-funding for local nodes, temples, or offerings without central grants. Aligns capital access with moral and service participation rather than wealth.

Concept: An alchemical farming process that unites financial liquidity (stOFFER, LP) with creative/ritual energy (SHROOM). Rewards minted as: PSILO tokens (cultural yield) Rare NFTs (unique “fruit” art pieces) PoB and Gratitude boosts (soul-level yield) Purpose Encourage balanced engagement: liquidity + artistry + service. Tie aesthetic creation to token emission so yield is not merely financial.

The burn triggers: Increase in PoB score (proof of renunciation). Possible minting of a “Votive NFT” — a permanent badge of offering. Reduced overall token supply (deflationary effect). Purpose Keeps circulation in check while enshrining altruism. Symbolically represents purification: giving up possession for presence.

Create a Markdown file at docs/hello.md: docs/hello.md # Hello This is my **first Docusaurus document**! A new document is now available at http://localhost:3000/docs/hello.

Docusaurus automatically creates a sidebar from the docs folder. Add metadata to customize the sidebar label and position: docs/hello.md --- sidebar_label: 'Hi!' sidebar_position: 3 --- # Hello This is my **first Docusaurus document**! It is also possible to create our sidebar explicitly in sidebars.js: sidebars.js export default { tutorialSidebar: [ 'intro', 'hello', { type: 'category', label: 'Tutorial', items: ['tutorial-basics/create-a-document'], }, ], };

Docusaurus is a static-site-generator (also called Jamstack). It builds our site as simple static HTML, JavaScript and CSS files.
Build our site for production: npm run build The static files are generated in the build folder.

Test our production build locally: npm run serve The build folder is now served at http://localhost:3000/. we can now deploy the build folder almost anywhere easily, for free or very small cost (read the Deployment Guide).
Docusaurus supports Markdown and a few additional features.

Markdown documents have metadata at the top called Front Matter: my-doc.md --- id: my-doc-id title: My document title description: My document description slug: /my-custom-url --- ## Markdown heading Markdown text with [links](./hello.md)

Regular Markdown links are supported, using url paths or relative file paths. Let's see how to [Create a page](/create-a-page). Let's see how to [Create a page](./create-a-page.md). Result: Let's see how to Create a page.

Regular Markdown images are supported. we can use absolute paths to reference images in the static directory (static/img/docusaurus.png): ![Docusaurus logo](/img/docusaurus.png) we can reference images relative to the current file as well. This is particularly useful to colocate images close to the Markdown files using them: ![Docusaurus logo](./img/docusaurus.png)
